interval: v1 retains entry-stop exclusive semantics; v2 stage_enter to stage_exit includes the final stage, including equal-stage intervals. Native recording and telemetry consume bounded ranges; navigation starts at accepted START and can stop once at a later boundary. Preparation remains fixed to its existing owner.
once_semantics: Request once per runtime instance; completion/failure must be reported explicitly, never inferred from a single invocation
parameter_source: Project algorithm_parameters and plugin actual-value contract; bindings do not copy parameters
backend: Adapter declarations preserve installed manifest identities. Supported native ranges and dependencies are generated as fixed owner tables; unsupported schedules remain explicit generation errors.
input_authority: FunctionsConfiguration_Apply transactionally reconciles user-selectable physical inputs through canonical capability_source_overrides and all related source groups. Function cards cannot create a second device-routing authority.
native_dependency_semantics: Recording and telemetry may require INS and/or estimator output. Every dependency must cover the entire configured interval and be initialized, running, healthy and no older than 100 ms when the consumer reads it. Cached readiness expires even if FlightTask stops updating. Control ACKs, identity and stage events remain serviced.

adapters.runtime_contract: Fixed preflight lifecycle; no arbitrary phase scheduling. Completion and failure remain owned by the existing preparation service.

condition_source_semantics: The first selected project navigation strategy owns numeric condition signals. Its output must be available before entry-condition sampling; producer start at the same entry cannot satisfy it.
external_event_semantics: Events such as launch_detected are supplied by their authoritative producer; this adapter does not infer an estimator dependency from an event or stage name.
reference_snapshot_order: One validated state/time snapshot: evaluate entry condition, commit at most one stage transition, stop intervals, start intervals in dependency order, then return each continuous instance once. No algorithm/hardware execution is inferred.
